correctness.summary: The disproof is correct and can be seen even more directly than stated. The sharp fractional isoperimetric inequality gives P_s(E_i)>=P_s(B) for each unit-volume chamber, while two far-separated unit balls are admissible; hence the infimum of the sum functional is exactly m_s=2 P_s(B) for every s, not merely asymptotically. BBM then gives (1-s)m_s->omega T. The independent geometry check reproduced T=9.6719517, C_0=9.1394217 and S_0=10.1549130, with gaps T-C_0=0.53253 and S_0-T=0.48296, so convergence to either classical double-bubble reading is impossible.

limitations: The result says nothing about minimizers of the standard fractional cluster energy in which all phases/interfaces are counted appropriately.
No L1 convergence or classification of fractional cluster minimizers is proved.
The repository text names output/artifacts/verify_gaps.py while the audited tree stores the script at artifacts/verify_gaps.py; this is a packaging-path defect only.
The theorem is largely a direct consequence of existing isoperimetric and BBM results.

originality.summary: The main limit follows immediately from the standard sharp fractional isoperimetric inequality plus the BBM limit, and the classical double-bubble constants are standard geometry. The record's originality is therefore low as a theorem. Its contribution is better understood as identifying a functional mismatch in the target: the sum P_s(E1)+P_s(E2) decouples chamberwise rather than approximating the shared-interface cluster energy.

scientific_value.summary: Despite limited novelty, the result is scientifically useful because it decisively falsifies the proposed rate and pinpoints the reason: the chosen energy is the wrong variational functional for a classical double bubble limit.
